questions.q: What is the central conflict that drives the primary theme of "The Enemy"?
questions.a: The central conflict is Dr. Sadao's dilemma between his duty as a doctor to save a wounded enemy soldier and his duty as a Japanese citizen to hand him over to the authorities. A wrong answer (e.g., "the conflict is between Sadao and the General") reveals the student is confusing a secondary plot point with the core thematic conflict.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the author uses the character of Hana to reinforce the primary theme.
questions.a: Hana initially shares the nationalistic prejudice but gradually supports Sadao's decision to help the soldier, showing that compassion can overcome ingrained hatred. Her internal struggle mirrors the theme. A wrong answer that says "Hana just obeys Sadao" misses her independent moral growth and the theme's emphasis on individual conscience.

questions.q: Apply the concept of 'primary theme' to a new situation: If the story were set in a modern conflict (e.g., a doctor in a war-torn country treating an enemy combatant), what would be the analogous thematic conflict?
questions.a: The analogous conflict would be between medical neutrality (the Hippocratic Oath) and pressure from the state or community to deny care to the enemy. The theme remains: professional ethics vs. national loyalty. A wrong answer that changes the theme to "love conquers all" shows failure to abstract the core conflict.

questions.q: Analyze how the General's character serves the primary theme. Compare his attitude with Sadao's.
questions.a: The General prioritizes his own survival over national duty (he offers assassins but forgets), exposing the hypocrisy of blind patriotism. Sadao, despite his prejudice, acts on professional ethics. The contrast highlights that true humanity is in action, not rhetoric. A wrong answer that calls the General "patriotic" misses the irony and thematic function.

questions.q: Evaluate whether the story's ending (Sadao helping the soldier escape) is the only possible resolution that honors the primary theme. Justify your view.
questions.a: Yes, because any other outcome (handing him over, killing him) would betray the medical ethic that the story upholds as superior to nationalism. The escape allows Sadao to fulfill both duties partially: he saves the soldier and protects his family. A wrong answer that says "he should have handed him over to be a true patriot" fails to evaluate the theme's hierarchy of values.

questions.q: Create a one-paragraph alternate ending where Sadao makes a different choice, and explain how that changes the primary theme.
questions.a: Example: Sadao turns the soldier over to the police. The soldier is executed. The theme shifts from "humanity over nationalism" to "nationalism destroys humanity." A good answer shows the thematic consequence. A poor answer just writes a plot change without linking to theme.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The primary theme of a literary work is the central idea or message that the author conveys through the narrative, ______, and conflicts.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are a doctor in a war zone and an enemy ______ is brought to you, bleeding.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can identify the primary theme of "The Enemy," trace its development through at least three key episodes in the story, and explain how the resolution reflects the author's message about humanity transcending national boundaries, using textual evidence in a structured answer (PEEL format).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you are a doctor in a war zone and an enemy soldier is brought to you, ______.
